Reason and Result Clauses Using Participles

When talking about the reasons for or the results of an action or a situation, you can use clauses introduced by conjunctions like because or since. However, to make your language use more varied, you can introduce reasons or results with participles.
Participles are words formed by the verb + ing and used as adjectives or nouns. You can use them as part of a reason or result clause.

For example:
Being preoccupied with my work, I forgot to eat lunch. (Reason)
Having finished my work, I decided to go on a long walk. (Result)
I like you taking the initiative.
There is going to be teacher's convention converging at the Hilton in Chicago.
Aren't events like these always demanding bookings made well in advance?
Seeing that this is kind of my idea, I would like to be a part of the sales team.
The Present Continuous and Be Going To
You use the Present Continuous tense to talk about a variety of situations. You use be going to to talk about the future.

images.text:
Denise: Adam, can you pop by my office? Because we need to discuss your proposal.
Adam: Sure.
Denise: Please, sit down. Don't mind the noise, they are working on something next door. So your e-mail said you have an idea to help us get more exposure for our new title, Winnie's World. I like you taking the initiative. Tell me more.

Adam: There is a nationwide teacher's convention in Chicago next week. There is going to be teachers and school board administrators from around the country converging at the Hilton in Chicago. They are going to be going to conferences, seminars and workshops for the entire week. During that time, there will be several publishers selling their merchandise and now that we have Winnie's World up and running, I think this conference would give us a great platform to sell this book. We've been working hard to get it ready and this could be a great opportunity. What do you think?
Denise: Since no one brought it up until now, I haven't considered it. Aren't we cutting it a little close? Aren't events like these always demanding bookings made well in advance?
Adam: I thought we were going to be cutting it a little close as well, but I talked to them today and it turns out, they had some last minute cancellations, so if we let them know by tomorrow, they would be able to accommodate us.
Denise: I'm intrigued. Good work.

Adam: Also, Denise. Um, I was wondering. Seeing that this is kind of my idea, I would like to be a part of the sales team. If that would be ok.
Denise: Ok. Adam, but there's just one thing. As the conference is in Chicago, and since we have a tight budget, we are going to need you to put in a funding request. So, I'd like you to write a funding request for me and have it ready by tomorrow. If we get funding, you can be part of the sales team.
Adam: Ok. I've never written one before.
Denise: Don't worry. Just take the ball and run with it.
